How to sew a lined fabric basket

A lined fabric basket from two squares of cotton: walls stiffened with interfacing, lace and bows glued on. Watch it come together step by step.

Some links on this page are affiliate links. As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.

Overview

The finished basket

A lined fabric basket: a cotton outer stiffened with interfacing, a cotton lining, and lace and bows glued on. Tap the basket to take it apart.

  1. 1Outer — cotton · a 60 × 60 cm (23⅝ in) square with a 20 × 20 cm (7⅞ in) square cut from every corner
  2. 2Interfacing ×5 — heavy, fusible · 19 × 19 cm (7½ in) squares on the base and the walls of the outer, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) in from the edges
  3. 3Lining — cotton · the same cross as the outer, without interfacing
  4. 4Ribbon — lace, or any ribbon · glued round the top with hot glue, the joint on a flat side
  5. 5Bows ×4 — one on every corner, glued on, a red half-bead in the middle
  6. 6Seams — all 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) · a 15 cm (5⅞ in) opening in a lining corner seam · topstitch 0.5 cm from the top edge

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Cut a 60 × 60 cm (23⅝ × 23⅝ in) square of cotton for the outer and another one for the lining.

    From every corner of both squares cut away a 20 × 20 cm (7⅞ × 7⅞ in) square. What is left is a cross: the square in the middle is the base, the four arms are the walls.

    From heavy fusible interfacing cut five squares, 19 × 19 cm (7½ × 7½ in): one for the base and one for each wall of the outer.

    Every seam allowance in this basket is 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in).

    The caption in the video says 50 × 50 cm — that is a mistake: the squares are 60 × 60 cm.

  2. Lay the outer cross wrong side up.

    Place a square of interfacing, glue side down, in the middle of the base and of each of the four walls — 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) in from the edges all round, so it stays out of the seams.

    Iron the squares on. The interfacing goes on the outer only, not on the lining.

  3. Turn the outer cross over, right side up.

    Fold the walls up so that the edges of two neighbouring walls meet, right sides together. Pin them.

    Sew the corner seam 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge, from the top edge right down to the point at the base. No backstitching.

    Sew all four corners. The outer is now a box, inside out — the interfacing is on the outside.

    Machine: straight stitch

  4. Fold up the walls of the lining cross, right sides together, and pin the edges that meet.

    Sew three corner seams 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge, from the top down to the point.

    Sew the fourth one too, but leave a 15 cm (5⅞ in) opening in it. It is this big because the interfaced walls of the outer are stiff and need room to come through.

    Keep the lining inside out.

    Machine: straight stitch

  5. Turn the outer right side out.

    Slip it into the lining, which stays inside out, so the right sides face each other. Line up the corner seams and the top edges.

    Sew all the way round the top, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge.

    Machine: straight stitch

  6. Pull the whole basket out through the 15 cm (5⅞ in) opening in the lining.

    Tuck in the raw edges of the opening and stitch it closed on the machine, close to the edge.

    Machine: straight stitch

  7. Push the lining down inside the basket, right into the corners.

    Topstitch all the way round the top, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge. The basket is done — the trim is up to you.

    Machine: straight stitch

  8. The trim is glued on with a hot glue gun, not sewn.

    Glue a ribbon all the way round the top. Put the joint on the flat of a wall, not on a corner.

    Glue a bow on each of the four corners. In the video they are made beforehand from white ribbon, with a red plastic half-bead glued in the middle — ready-made bows work just as well.

    Any ribbon in any width: lace for Christmas, as in the video; a plain black ribbon or an orange one with pumpkins for Halloween; or no trim at all for every day. The basket in the video holds tangerines on the Christmas table — use yours for anything you like.

Good to know

Questions and answers

How much fabric do I need for a fabric basket?

For this basket you need two 60 × 60 cm (23⅝ in) squares of cotton — one for the outer, one for the lining — and five 19 × 19 cm (7½ in) squares of heavy fusible interfacing. From every corner of both cotton squares cut away a 20 × 20 cm (7⅞ in) square. The cutting diagram below shows it all.

How do you make a fabric basket stand up?

With heavy fusible interfacing on the outer: five 19 × 19 cm (7½ in) squares, one in the middle of the base and of each wall, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) in from the edges, ironed onto the wrong side. The lining gets no interfacing.

How do you sew the corners of a fabric basket?

Fold up the walls of the cross so the edges of two neighbouring walls meet, right sides together. Pin them and sew 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge, from the top right down to the point at the base. Four corner seams make the box — first on the outer, then on the lining.

Where do you leave the opening to turn a lined basket?

In one corner seam of the lining: leave 15 cm (5⅞ in) unsewn. It is this big because the interfaced walls are stiff. Turn the basket right side out through it, then stitch the opening closed on the machine.

What seam allowance should I use for a fabric basket?

Every seam in this basket is 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in): the four corner seams of the outer and of the lining and the seam round the top. The topstitching round the top is 0.5 cm from the edge too.

How do you decorate a fabric basket for Christmas?

The trim is glued on with a hot glue gun, not sewn: a ribbon all round the top, with the joint on a flat side rather than on a corner, and a bow on every corner. In the video it is lace and white bows with a red half-bead in the middle. Any ribbon works — a black one, or an orange one with pumpkins for Halloween — or no trim at all.
